summary: Oregon Department of Education urges the FCC to keep E‑Rate robust, preserve both Category One and Two support, maintain cost‑effective special construction and state matching, keep need‑based statewide eligibility, separate screen‑time policy from connectivity funding, and adopt program‑integrity improvements. Oregon E‑Rate analysis argues that eliminating or reducing E‑Rate would force districts to absorb $40 million+ in two‑year costs, leading to larger classes, fewer teachers, and loss of services, especially in rural and high‑need areas. It also contends that both Category One and Category Two services are essential, and that special construction and state‑matching discounts should be preserved as cost‑effective solutions for schools that cannot be served by existing infrastructure. Oregon Department of Education (ODE) argues that special construction and state‑matching discounts should remain in place and that E‑Rate should not be limited to rural or single‑provider areas, citing the need for adequate, affordable broadband in remote districts.
